findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the OBSERVED real-pandoc 3.6.1 jira-writer output for at least one color ({color:name}) and one monospace ({{monospace}}) case in ADR 0095 (as already done for the heading form), so the monkeypatched fixtures are pinned to verified ground truth rather than the author's model.
evidence: Plan: 'monkeypatch only pypandoc.convert_text to return fixed successful Jira writer shapes from Markdown inputs, then exercise the real classifier on passes 2-5'

Contrast: plan records the real-pandoc heading form 'h1. {anchor:}Heading\n' in ADR 0095 from an empirical probe, and uses 'real pandoc first-pass outputs for bold, italic, and links' — but not for color/monospace
search_files confirms pypandoc is a new integration (no prior usage in repo); resolve_symbol pypandoc = UNRESOLVED (optional extra, not installed in this env — not probeable here)
findings.finding: The pandoc jira-writer output shapes for color ({color:name}...{color}) and monospace ({{monospace}}) are asserted from the author's model rather than observed from real pandoc: the plan monkeypatches pypandoc.convert_text to return 'fixed successful Jira writer shapes' for these two constructs because they 'have no suitable CommonMark source without conflicting with code preservation', while bold/italic/link use real first-pass pandoc output. These two specific writer surfaces are therefore Partially-verified — the integration (pandoc jira writer) is real and version-pinned, but the exact emitted form for color/monospace is unconfirmed against the real binary, unlike the heading form which the ADR 0095 probe recorded verbatim.
findings.location: Renderer contract — 'For color and monospace, which have no suitable CommonMark source... monkeypatch only pypandoc.convert_text to return fixed successful Jira writer shapes'
scenarios: Real pandoc 3.6.1's jira writer emits a color/monospace form that differs from the monkeypatched fixture (e.g. different color-name casing, spacing, or attribute rendering), so the passthrough recognizer's assumptions about what pandoc produces are never validated against ground truth
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the ADR 0095 pin/provenance section the real `commonmark -> jira --wrap=none` output captured from the clean-environment probe for a color-marked and a monospace-marked input, and derive the monkeypatch fixtures from those recorded strings so the Partially-verified surface becomes Verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify phase-1 lock behavior for unterminated openers: state whether a lone `<!--`, an unclosed fence, or an unclosed `{noformat}` locks to EOF or is treated as ordinary text, and add a passthrough/five-pass test covering an unterminated protected-span opener.
evidence: Plan locks 'complete `{noformat}` spans' and comments 'from `<!--` through the next `-->`' but says nothing about what happens when the closer never appears

An unterminated `<!--` could otherwise expose the arrow pass (which itself special-cases `<!--`/`-->`) or the HTML-tag classifier to a partial marker, risking a non-byte-identical transform of protected content
The per-unit byte-identity fallback ('Every extracted fragment must appear byte-identically ... or that unit falls back') may catch this, but the intended lock boundary is left ambiguous
findings.finding: Phase-1 lock semantics are specified only for COMPLETE protected spans; the unterminated-opener edge case (a lone `<!--` with no following `-->`, or an unclosed fence/`{noformat}` opener) has undefined segmentation behavior — unclear whether the lock extends to EOF or the opener falls through into later classifiers and arrow substitution.
findings.location: Renderer contract, phase 1 ("Lock complete `{noformat}` spans, HTML comments from `<!--` through the next `-->`, backtick/tilde fences")
scenarios: A body containing a stray `<!--` fragment (e.g. inside prose discussing HTML) with no matching `-->`
A code body whose fence opener is unbalanced across the truncation boundary

findings.finding: The plan adds a second, heavier Markdown-conversion toolchain (pypandoc-binary==1.15 bundling pandoc 3.6.1) for the DC wiki renderer, while the sibling in-family Cloud converter (story e59d, referenced by rebar:3388) already adopted marklas + mistune as the family's Markdown-aware engine behind a lazy optional extra. The alternatives analysis rejects only three jira-specific libraries (md-to-jira, mistune-jira, md-jira) and never reconciles the choice against the marklas/mistune stack already in the jira_family, leaving two parallel Markdown engines across the Cloud/DC sides of one adapter family.

scenarios: A future reader/maintainer must reason about two different Markdown parse/convert engines (pandoc vs marklas+mistune) within one jira_family adapter, doubling the fidelity/round-trip/edge-case surface

findings.finding: The HTML-comment classifier (classifier 4) specifies the pattern `<[/!]?[A-Za-z][^>]*>`, which requires the character immediately following `</`, `<!`, or `<` to be `[A-Za-z]`. In an HTML comment `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` the character after `<!` is `-`, not a letter, so the pattern does NOT match. A body unit consisting of (or containing only) an HTML comment falls through classifiers 1-4, and if it also passes classifiers 2, 3, and 5 (no Jira markup, no ASCII table, no regex-dangerous content), it lands in classifier 6 where pandoc deletes it — exactly the `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` deletion the plan's Problem section names as the primary motivator. The arrow-substitution step that maps `<!--`/`-->` 'to themselves' runs before the pandoc call, not after, so it cannot rescue a comment that pandoc deletes.
findings.location: Renderer contract section — classifier 4: 'HTML comment or tag matching `<[/!]?[A-Za-z][^>]*>`'; Acceptance Criteria: 'HTML comments survive exactly; corpus HTML test'
findings.suggested_fix: Add HTML comment locking to the phase-1 lexer: lock spans matching `<!--.*?-->` (with `re.DOTALL`) alongside `{noformat}` spans and backtick fences, so they are treated as 'already locked' blocks that pass exactly in classifier 1, never reaching pandoc.
